title: Sunny and the Peacock Spider | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka spots the tiniest, most colourful creature in the whole bush — a peacock spider — resting on a leaf in the moonlight, its brilliant pattern folded away for the night. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The spider was the size of a rice grain.

Sunny saw it because a dewdrop on the leaf beside it caught the moonlight, and in looking at the dewdrop she looked at the leaf, and on the leaf — impossibly small, impossibly still — was something that should not have existed.

A peacock spider.

Even in the moonlight, even with its fan folded flat and hidden, she could see the colours — a small glimpse at the edge of its abdomen. Orange. Blue. Something red. Colours so vivid they seemed impossible on something so small.

She pressed her nose almost to the leaf.

The spider did not move. It was resting — abdomen fan closed, four of its eight eyes visible, watching the world even in sleep with the quiet vigilance of something very small in a world of large things.

She thought: it is the smallest artist in the whole bush. It wears a painting on its back.

She held very still.

The peacock spider stayed very still.

For a long time they were both very still together — the most colourful creature in the bush and the small quokka who had found it — sharing the moonlit leaf in the dark.

She thought: the world is so much bigger than it looks, if you know where to look.

She fell asleep right there.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, peacock spider. Goodnight, little one.
